most_likely: Postprocedural hemorrhage from vaginal cuff following total laparoscopic hysterectomy
summary: Woman ~3 weeks status post exam under anesthesia, extensive lysis of adhesions, total laparoscopic hysterectomy with bilateral salpingectomy and cystoscopy, presenting with acute heavy vaginal bleeding with clots after an initial period of only light spotting. Clinic exam showed no cuff dehiscence and a small bleeding vessel was cauterized; pelvic ultrasound showed a normal vaginal cuff with no hematoma. Hematocrit 38.1 (preop 40.1), hemodynamically stable, no procedure required this stay; bleeding decreased with observation and she was discharged on hospital day 2.

differential.diagnosis: Postprocedural hemorrhage from vaginal cuff following total laparoscopic hysterectomy
supporting_evidence: Chief complaint: heavy vaginal bleeding after hysterectomy
Small vessel at cuff cauterized in clinic
TLH/BS with extensive lysis of adhesions ~3 weeks prior
opposing_evidence: No transfusion or operative intervention required
differential.reasoning: Bleeding is directly attributable to the recent hysterectomy site with an identified cuff vessel cauterized; this is the principal disease driving the admission for observation.
